scope: ADDITIVE to spec/design-tokens.json and spec/settings-tokens.json. The Mock Lab introduces NO new colour tokens — it is built entirely from the existing set. What is new is four patterns.
restraint: Deliberate. A screen this size would normally accrete tokens; every meaning here maps onto a token that already carries it, so adding more would dilute the ones that exist.

tokensUsed.--txt: filled frequency dots and the prediction marker

newPatterns.name: Dual-signal calibration row
newPatterns.structure: 10 dots (filled = observed frequency, outlined = remainder) + a ▲ marker beneath, positioned at the stated probability index
newPatterns.markerMath: left = (stated/100 * 10 * dotPitch) - 4px, where dotPitch = 14px (11px dot + 3px gap)
newPatterns.reading: ▲ left of the fill edge = under-confident; right = over-confident; under the edge = honest
newPatterns.rationale: reuses the existing 10-dot frequency idiom rather than introducing a second visual language for probability

newPatterns.name: Progress-to-target array
newPatterns.structure: 30 squares, 15×15px, radius 3px, filled --acc when logged, outlined --line2 when not
newPatterns.rule: the array is never the primary progress signal — the confidence-band width above it is. No badges, streaks, levels or congratulation.
newPatterns.rationale: the honest incentive already exists: filling a square narrows the band

newPatterns.name: Confidence-band ladder
newPatterns.structure: one row per sample-size milestone (1 / 10 / 20 / 30 mocks): count, bar, ± half-width, plain label
newPatterns.math: bar length is the real 95% Wilson half-width at that n on a 33% bucket
newPatterns.rationale: motivation by measurement — the bar is a fact, not a graphic

newPatterns.name: Frozen-prediction marker
newPatterns.structure: 🔒 glyph + --up eyebrow + a left rule, on a banner rather than a footnote
newPatterns.rule: any surface showing a prediction as-made must state that it is never recomputed
newPatterns.rationale: a wrong prediction is the most valuable row on the screen; hiding it breaks the premise

verdictTreatment.rule: glyph carries the verdict in greyscale; colour is redundant

entryTempo.rule: a measurement, not a motivator — if entered_at is not recorded, remove the readout rather than estimate it
